title: Warsaw Hole / 50 Fathom Hole spawning SMZ: no snapper-grouper by any gear, no anchoring
effect: A square about 1.3 nm on a side, roughly 25 nm west-southwest of Key West, where no snapper-grouper may be taken by any gear (spear included) and a fishing vessel may not anchor, until 2 Aug 2027 unless extended.
excerpt: Any fishing vessel in a spawning SMZ is prohibited to fish for or harvest species in the snapper-grouper fishery management unit year-round. For a fishing vessel to possess snapper-grouper species on board while in a spawning SMZ, the vessel must be in transit and fishing gear must be appropriately stowed, as specified in paragraph (a)(2)(vii) of this section. Except for spawning SMZs of Area 51 and Area 53, the spawning SMZs in this paragraph are effective until August 2, 2027. A person on board a fishing vessel may not anchor, use an anchor and chain, or use a grapple and chain while in the spawning SMZs specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section. The anchoring prohibition does not apply to fishing vessels in the spawning SMZs of Area 51 and Area 53.
scope: Warsaw Hole/50 Fathom Hole Spawning SMZ, § 622.183(a)(2)(vi): rhumb lines A 24°22.277′N 82°20.417′W, B 24°22.277′N 82°18.215′W, C 24°20.932′N 82°18.215′W, D 24°20.932′N 82°20.417′W, back to A. The only one of the five spawning SMZs off Florida (the others are off North and South Carolina).
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. SUNSET: the Warsaw Hole SMZ is effective until 2 Aug 2027. The SAFMC is developing Snapper Grouper Regulatory Amendment 39 on the sunsetting of spawning SMZs (council meeting notices, Federal Register 18 Feb, 21 May, 17 Aug and 28 Aug 2026). Re-check after the SAFMC acts and before 2 Aug 2027. Regulatory Amendment 36 (final rule 91 FR, 28 Sep 2026, doc. 2026-19801, effective 28 Oct 2026) revises the transit gear-stowage text in (a)(2)(vii) for sea bass pots only; no effect on divers. 'Fishing vessel' is not defined in part 622; the conservative reading treats any boat carrying a spearfisher as a fishing vessel for the anchoring ban.

title: Florida artificial-reef SMZs: spearfishing banned at Ft. Pierce Inshore and Key Biscayne AR-H
effect: Two federal artificial-reef SMZs off Florida ban spearfishing gear outright (Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef, Key Biscayne/Artificial Reef H); a third (Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef) allows it.
excerpt: (a)(1)(xix) and (a)(1)(xxi): Use of spearfishing gear is prohibited.
full: To determine what restrictions apply in the SMZs listed in paragraph (a)(1) of this section, follow this table: (a)(1)(i) through (x) and (a)(1)(xxii) through (xxxix): Use of a powerhead to take South Atlantic snapper-grouper is prohibited. Possession of a powerhead and a mutilated South Atlantic snapper-grouper in, or after having fished in, one of these SMZs constitutes prima facie evidence that such fish was taken with a powerhead in the SMZ. Harvest and possession of a South Atlantic snapper-grouper is limited to the bag limits specified in § 622.187(b). (a)(1)(i) through (xviii) and (a)(1)(xxii) through (li): Fishing may only be conducted with handline, rod and reel, and spearfishing gear. (a)(1)(i) through (li): Use of a sea bass pot or bottom longline is prohibited. (a)(1)(xii) through (xviii) and (a)(1)(xl) through (li): Possession of South Atlantic snapper-grouper taken with a powerhead is limited to the bag limits specified in § 622.187(b). (a)(1)(xix) and (a)(1)(xx): A hydraulic or electric reel that is permanently affixed to the vessel is prohibited when fishing for South Atlantic snapper-grouper. (a)(1)(xix) and (a)(1)(xxi): Use of spearfishing gear is prohibited.
scope: Only three of the 51 South Atlantic SMZs lie off Florida: (xix) Ft. Pierce Inshore Reef, N 27°26.8′, S 27°25.8′, E 80°09.24′W, W 80°10.36′W; (xx) Ft. Pierce Offshore Reef, A 27°23.68′N 80°03.95′W, B 27°22.80′N 80°03.60′W, C 27°23.94′N 80°00.02′W, D 27°24.85′N 80°00.33′W; (xxi) Key Biscayne/Artificial Reef H, N 25°42.82′, S 25°41.32′, E 80°04.22′W, W 80°05.53′W. (xlvi) Artificial Reef KBY and (xlviii) Artificial Reef MRY lie just north of the Florida/Georgia line (30°45.5′N to 30°48.6′N) and allow handline, rod and reel and spearfishing gear only.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. The spearfishing row in table 2 is not limited to snapper-grouper on its face, so it is drawn as a ban on all spearfishing inside (xix) and (xxi) (the reading that closes more water). The powerhead ban row covers (i) to (x) and (xxii) to (xxxix) only, none off Florida. Rows applying to (xix) and (xx): 'A hydraulic or electric reel that is permanently affixed to the vessel is prohibited when fishing for South Atlantic snapper-grouper.' Row applying to (i) to (li): 'Use of a sea bass pot or bottom longline is prohibited.' The Key Biscayne box's west edge is about 3 nm off the beach; check whether any part lies in state waters.

title: South Atlantic EEZ: no spearing snapper-grouper while on a rebreather
effect: In federal waters off the Florida east coast and Keys, a diver on a rebreather may not spear any snapper-grouper species; open-circuit scuba and freediving are unaffected.
excerpt: (b) Rebreathers and spearfishing gear. In the South Atlantic EEZ, a person using a rebreather may not harvest South Atlantic snapper-grouper with spearfishing gear. The possession of such snapper-grouper while in the water with a rebreather is prima facie evidence that such fish was harvested with spearfishing gear while using a rebreather.
scope: South Atlantic EEZ only (east coast of Florida and the Atlantic side of the Keys). No equivalent rule in the Gulf EEZ: an eCFR title 50 search for 'rebreather' returns only this section.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Snapper-grouper species list is table 2 of appendix A to part 622 (includes hogfish, groupers, snappers, black sea bass, triggerfish, amberjacks, porgies).

title: Hogfish closed in federal waters off the Keys and east coast, November through April
effect: No recreational hogfish harvest or possession from the federal waters off the Keys and the Florida east coast (and Gulf federal waters south of 25°09′N) in January to April and November to December.
excerpt: Hogfish recreational sector off the Florida Keys and east coast of Florida. From January through April and from November through December each year, the recreational harvest or possession of hogfish in or from the South Atlantic EEZ off the Florida Keys and east coast of Florida, and in the Gulf EEZ south of 25°09′ N. lat. off the west coast of Florida is prohibited, and the bag and possession limits are zero.
scope: South Atlantic EEZ off the Keys and east coast; Gulf EEZ south of 25°09′N. Size limit 16 inches fork length in the same waters, § 622.185(c)(3)(ii). § 622.34(g) cross-refers here for the Gulf portion.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Hogfish is taken almost entirely by spear, so this is a spearfishing season in practice. State-water hogfish seasons are set separately by FWC; compare regs.json 'seasons' before publishing.

title: Goliath, Nassau, speckled hind and warsaw grouper: no harvest in federal waters
effect: These four groupers may not be taken or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ (Nassau also in the Gulf EEZ), by any gear including spear.
excerpt: Goliath grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ. [...] Speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be harvested or possessed in or from the South Atlantic EEZ. [...] Nassau grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ.
full: (b)(1) Goliath grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ. Goliath grouper taken in the South Atlantic EEZ incidentally by hook-and-line must be released immediately by cutting the line without removing the fish from the water. (b)(3) Speckled hind and warsaw grouper may not be harvested or possessed in or from the South Atlantic EEZ. Such fish caught in the South Atlantic EEZ must be released immediately with a minimum of harm. These restrictions also apply in the South Atlantic on board a vessel for which a valid Federal commercial or charter vessel/headboat permit for South Atlantic snapper-grouper has been issued, i.e., in state or Federal waters. (b)(4) Nassau grouper may not be harvested or possessed in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ. Nassau grouper taken in the South Atlantic EEZ or the Gulf EEZ incidentally by hook-and-line must be released immediately by cutting the line without removing the fish from the water.
scope: South Atlantic EEZ; Nassau grouper also Gulf EEZ. The Gulf goliath grouper rule was not located in § 622.32 (which only bans poisons); find its current section before citing a Gulf goliath prohibition.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Goliath grouper has a limited state-water harvest by FWC permit since 2023; the federal EEZ prohibition is unchanged. Speckled hind and warsaw grouper restrictions also apply in state waters aboard a vessel with a federal snapper-grouper commercial or charter permit ((b)(3) last sentence).

title: South Atlantic EEZ: descending device must be aboard, spearfishing boats included
effect: A boat whose divers are spearing or holding snapper-grouper in South Atlantic federal waters must carry a rigged descending device; the text has no spearfishing exemption.
excerpt: (4) Descending device. At least one descending device is required to be on board a vessel and be ready for use while fishing for or possessing South Atlantic snapper-grouper.
scope: South Atlantic EEZ.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Not a closure, an equipment rule. The text does not exempt spearfishing; the conservative reading is that it applies. § 622.188(b) lists spearfishing gear among the only authorized gear types for snapper-grouper. The Gulf equivalent, § 622.30(c) (DESCEND Act), states it was 'effective until January 14, 2026' and has lapsed; NOAA Fisheries' action page (read 30 Sep 2026, secondary) says a framework action to continue it was proposed 30 Jul 2026. Currency watch.

title: Oculina experimental closed area: no snapper-grouper, spear included
effect: Inside the Oculina Bank HAPC, the box from 27°30′N to 27°53′N and 79°56′W to 80°00′W is closed to fishing for snapper-grouper by any gear, spearfishing included, and none may be retained.
excerpt: Within the Oculina Bank HAPC, the experimental closed area is bounded on the north by 27°53′ N. lat., on the south by 27°30′ N. lat., on the east by 79°56′ W. long., and on the west by 80°00' W. long. No person may fish for South Atlantic snapper-grouper in the experimental closed area, and no person may retain South Atlantic snapper-grouper in or from the area.
scope: Off Fort Pierce and Vero Beach, 60 to 100 m depth; inside the Oculina Bank HAPC so the HAPC anchoring ban also applies.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Split out of cfr-622-224 because that entry's effect ('NOT a spearfishing closure') is wrong for this paragraph. The eCFR prints the west bound as 80°00' with a straight apostrophe; reproduced as printed.

title: Dolphin and wahoo: spearfishing, powerheads included, is authorized gear in the Atlantic EEZ
effect: Spearing dolphin (mahi) and wahoo in Atlantic federal waters is lawful, and powerheads are expressly allowed for these two species.
excerpt: Except as allowed in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, the following are the only authorized gear types in the fishery for dolphin and wahoo in the Atlantic EEZ: Automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, pelagic longline, rod and reel, and spearfishing gear (including powerheads).
scope: Atlantic EEZ.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Kept as a positive rule because divers ask. 50 C.F.R. § 600.725(v) lists spear and powerhead for the South Atlantic snapper-grouper and Gulf reef fish recreational fisheries too (see cfr-600-725). For king and Spanish mackerel and cobia see cfr-622-375-a.

title: Federal list of authorized gear: spear and powerhead listed for recreational reef fish
effect: Spearfishing is an authorized federal recreational gear for South Atlantic snapper-grouper, Gulf reef fish and coastal migratory pelagics; a spear used on king or Spanish mackerel in the Atlantic is outside the § 622.375 gear list but the only consequence is that the bag limit applies.
excerpt: South Atlantic Snapper-Grouper Fishery, Recreational fishery: Handline, rod and reel, bandit gear, spear, powerhead. Gulf Reef Fish Fishery, Recreational fishery: Spear, powerhead, bandit gear, handline, rod reel, cast net.
scope: Federal EEZ, South Atlantic and Gulf councils.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Rows read from the govinfo annual edition (revised as of 1 Oct 2025); the current eCFR page truncated before the South Atlantic and Gulf rows, and eCFR search shows a version of § 600.725 effective 6 Apr 2026. Re-read the current rows in a browser before citing. Related: § 622.375(a)(1)(i)(B) limits Atlantic-group king mackerel south of Cape Lookout to automatic reel, bandit gear, handline and rod and reel, and (b)(3) makes a person aboard with unauthorized gear subject to the bag limits, which a recreational diver is under anyway.

title: King mackerel: spear is not an authorized federal gear (Atlantic south of Cape Lookout, and Gulf)
effect: In federal waters off Florida a spear is not on the gear list for king mackerel (Atlantic or Gulf group) or Atlantic-group Spanish mackerel; a diver who spears one is held to the recreational bag limit, which is the limit a recreational diver has anyway.
excerpt: (1) King and Spanish mackerel. Subject to the prohibitions on gear/methods specified in § 622.9, the following are the only fishing gears that may be used in the Gulf, Mid-Atlantic, and South Atlantic EEZ in directed fisheries for king and Spanish mackerel: (i) King mackerel, Atlantic migratory group—[...] (B) South of 34°37.3′ N. lat.—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, and rod and reel. (ii) King mackerel, Gulf migratory group—hook-and-line gear and, in the southern zone only, run-around gillnet. [...] (iii) Spanish mackerel, Atlantic migratory group—automatic reel, bandit gear, handline, rod and reel, cast net, run-around gillnet, and stab net. (iv) Spanish mackerel, Gulf migratory group—all gear except drift gillnet, long gillnet, and purse seine.
scope: Gulf, Mid-Atlantic and South Atlantic EEZ. Gulf-group cobia ((a)(2), which covers the Gulf EEZ and the South Atlantic EEZ south of a line due east from the Florida/Georgia border): all gear except drift gillnet and long gillnet, so spearing cobia is authorized.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (b)(3): 'Except as specified in paragraph (b)(4) of this section, a person aboard a vessel with unauthorized gear other than a drift gillnet in the Gulf EEZ or a long gillnet on board in, or that has fished in, the EEZ where such gear is not authorized in paragraph (a) of this section, is subject to the bag limits for king and Spanish mackerel specified in § 622.382(a)(1)(ii) and (iv), respectively, and to the limit on cobia specified in § 622.383(b).' CONFLICT to flag: § 600.725(v) (govinfo 2025 edition) lists 'spear' as authorized gear for the South Atlantic and Gulf coastal migratory pelagics recreational fisheries. 'Directed fisheries' is undefined in § 622.375. Practical reading for the map: spearing king or Atlantic Spanish mackerel in the EEZ is not a closure; the consequence is the bag limit. Not a map feature; a sidebar note.

cite: 50 C.F.R. § 622.35(a)(1); app. B to pt. 622, table 2
title: Gulf reef fish stressed area: no powerheads (spearguns fine)
effect: In the band of Gulf federal waters between state waters and a line running from the Tortugas to the Alabama line, powerheads may not be used on reef fish; ordinary spearguns are not restricted.
excerpt: (1) A powerhead may not be used in the stressed area to take Gulf reef fish. Possession of a powerhead and a mutilated Gulf reef fish in the stressed area or after having fished in the stressed area constitutes prima facie evidence that such reef fish was taken with a powerhead in the stressed area.
scope: 'The stressed area is that part of the Gulf EEZ shoreward of rhumb lines connecting, in order, the points listed in Table 2 in Appendix B of this part.' Florida points 1 to 15: 1 24°45.5′N 82°41.5′W (NE of Dry Tortugas) through 15 29°34.5′N 87°38.0′W (south of the Florida and Alabama border).
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Powerhead is defined at § 622.2: 'any device with an explosive charge, usually attached to a speargun, spear, pole, or stick, that fires a projectile upon contact.' Map as a line with a warn popup; the landward edge is the state waters boundary (9 nm off the Gulf coast). The only other Gulf spearfishing text in § 622.35 is the Alabama SMZ (d), which lies wholly off Alabama (easternmost point 87°55.5′W, west of the Florida line): confirmed negative for Florida.

title: Gulf coral HAPCs off Florida: NOT a spearfishing rule, but some ban anchoring
effect: Florida Middle Grounds bans only bottom longline, trawl, dredge, pot and trap; Tortugas North and South ban all fishing and anchoring by fishing vessels; Pulley Ridge South, Pulley Ridge South Portion A and West Florida Wall ban bottom gear and anchoring by fishing vessels.
excerpt: Deployment of a bottom longline, bottom trawl, dredge, pot, or trap is prohibited year-round in the area bounded by rhumb lines connecting the following points in order: [Florida Middle Grounds HAPC, (a)]
scope: Florida Middle Grounds (a): A 28°42.500′N 84°24.800′W, B 28°42.500′N 84°16.300′W, C 28°11.000′N 84°00.000′W, D 28°11.000′N 84°07.000′W, E 28°26.600′N 84°24.800′W. Pulley Ridge South (c), Pulley Ridge South Portion A (d), West Florida Wall (e), Tortugas marine reserves HAPC (b). Coordinates in geometry.json.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Intro text: 'For the purposes of this section, fishing gear is deployed if any part of the gear is in contact with the water.' (b): 'Fishing for any species and bottom anchoring by fishing vessels are prohibited year-round in the areas of the HAPC.' (c): 'Deployment of a bottom longline, bottom trawl, buoy gear, dredge, pot, or trap, and bottom anchoring by fishing vessels are prohibited year-round in the area of the HAPC bounded by rhumb lines connecting the following points in order:' The Florida Middle Grounds has NO anchoring ban and no diver rule, a confirmed negative worth stating because it is a popular spearfishing destination. § 622.74(b)(1) cites NOAA chart 11434 for the Tortugas North state-waters edge while § 622.410(a) cites chart 11438: an inconsistency inside the CFR.

title: Highly migratory species: spearguns only for yellowfin, bigeye, albacore and skipjack tuna
effect: In federal waters a speargun may be used on BAYS tunas (bigeye, albacore, yellowfin, skipjack) only, from a boat with an HMS Angling or Charter/Headboat permit, diver in the water, no powerheads; spearing bluefin tuna, billfish, swordfish or sharks is prohibited.
excerpt: (h) Speargun fishing gear. Speargun fishing gear may only be utilized when recreational fishing for Atlantic BAYS tunas and only from vessels issued either a valid HMS Angling or valid HMS Charter/Headboat permit. Persons fishing for Atlantic BAYS tunas using speargun gear, as specified in § 635.19, must be physically in the water when the speargun is fired or discharged, and may freedive, use SCUBA, or other underwater breathing devices. Only free-swimming BAYS tunas, not those restricted by fishing lines or other means, may be taken by speargun fishing gear. "Powerheads," as defined at § 600.10 of this chapter, or any other explosive devices, may not be used to harvest or fish for BAYS tunas with speargun fishing gear.
full: § 635.71(b)(30) Fish for any HMS, other than Atlantic BAYS tunas, with speargun fishing gear, as specified at § 635.21(h). (31) Harvest or fish for BAYS tunas using speargun gear with powerheads, or any other explosive devices, as specified in § 635.21(h). (32) Sell, purchase, barter for, or trade for an Atlantic BAYS tuna harvested with speargun fishing gear, as specified at § 635.31(a)(1). (33) Fire or discharge speargun gear without being physically in the water, as specified at § 635.21(h). (34) Use speargun gear to harvest a BAYS tuna restricted by fishing lines or other means, as specified at § 635.21(h). (35) Use speargun gear to fish for BAYS tunas from a vessel that does not possess either a valid HMS Angling or HMS Charter/Headboat category permit, as specified at § 635.21(h).
scope: Atlantic HMS management area, which includes the Gulf and Caribbean. Speargun fishing gear is defined at § 635.2 as a muscle-powered speargun with a trigger, a spear designed to penetrate and retain fish, and terminal gear.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. § 635.71(b)(30): 'Fish for any HMS, other than Atlantic BAYS tunas, with speargun fishing gear, as specified at § 635.21(h).' (b)(32): BAYS tuna taken by speargun may not be sold. § 635.19(c) billfish and sailfish: rod and reel only; (d) sharks: rod and reel or handline only; (e) swordfish (recreational): handline or rod and reel only. This matches the state ban on spearing sharks and billfish in r. 68B-20.005. Federal HMS permit and tuna reporting obligations apply to the vessel.

title: Spiny lobster: no spears or hooks in federal waters
effect: A spiny lobster may not be speared or hooked in federal waters, and a speared or punctured lobster aboard is presumed illegally taken.
excerpt: A spiny lobster may not be taken in the EEZ with a spear, hook, or similar device, or gear containing such devices. In the EEZ, the possession of a speared, pierced, or punctured spiny lobster is prima facie evidence that prohibited gear was used to take such lobster.
scope: Gulf and South Atlantic EEZ (subpart R, spiny lobster fishery). Part 697 (American lobster) also bans spearing, § 697.7, but American lobster does not occur off Florida.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. Mirrors the state prohibition. The remaining sentence of (a) excludes a hook in a hook-and-line fishery for other species. Paragraph (e) bans simultaneous possession of a bully net and underwater breathing apparatus aboard a commercial lobster vessel in the EEZ off Florida (commercial only).

title: Refuges not listed in part 32 are closed to fishing, including spearfishing
effect: Taking any animal on a national wildlife refuge is prohibited unless part 32 opens that refuge; sixteen Florida refuges are opened and the rest (Key West, Great White Heron, National Key Deer, Crystal River, Crocodile Lake, Passage Key, Pine Island, Matlacha Pass, Island Bay, Archie Carr, among others) are not.
excerpt: No person shall take any animal or plant on any national wildlife refuge, except as authorized under 50 CFR 27.51 and parts 31, 32, and 33 of this subchapter C.
scope: § 32.7(i) Florida list: Arthur R. Marshall Loxahatchee, Cedar Keys, Chassahowitzka, Egmont Key, Everglades Headwaters, Florida Panther, Hobe Sound, J.N. "Ding" Darling, Lake Woodruff, Lower Suwannee, Merritt Island, Pelican Island, Pinellas, St. Marks, St. Vincent, Ten Thousand Islands.
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. CONFLICT, unresolved: the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's own Key West NWR and Great White Heron NWR pages (fws.gov, read 30 Sep 2026) say 'Sport and commercial fishing in accordance with state fishing laws' and that refuge waters are open 24 hours for fishing, snorkeling and diving. The submerged lands there are state-owned and co-managed under the 1992 Backcountry Management Agreement, so they may not be refuge 'waters administered by FWS' within § 25.12. Drawn as warn, not closed, with this conflict stated; the conservative reading (closed) rests on the CFR text alone. Passage Key NWR, Pine Island NWR, Matlacha Pass NWR, Island Bay NWR and Crocodile Lake NWR are posted by FWS as closed to the public; for Pine Island, Matlacha Pass and Island Bay the refuge is the islands, and the surrounding water is a state aquatic preserve (FWS pages), so the water is not closed by the refuge. § 26.21(a): 'No person shall trespass, including but not limited to entering, occupying, using, or being upon, any national wildlife refuge, except as specifically authorized in this subchapter C or in other applicable Federal regulations.'

title: Hobe Sound NWR: rods and reels and poles and lines only, so no spearfishing
effect: Fishing on Hobe Sound NWR (including its Jupiter Island beach) is limited to rods and reels and poles and lines, sunrise to sunset, which excludes spearfishing from refuge lands and waters.
excerpt: (iii) We allow the use of only rods and reels and poles and lines, and anglers must attend them at all times.
scope: Hobe Sound NWR, Martin County: Jupiter Island beach unit and Indian River Lagoon mainland unit. The refuge's seaward boundary was not checked; if it stops at mean high water, the rule governs shore entry through the refuge rather than the water itself.

title: Dry Tortugas Research Natural Area: closed to all fishing and anchoring
effect: The 46-square-mile Research Natural Area in the northwest of the park is closed to all fishing, anchoring is banned, and boats must use the mooring buoys.
excerpt: The following waters and areas are closed to fishing: (i) The Research Natural Area (RNA): Fish and fishing gear may be possessed aboard a vessel in the RNA, provided such fish can be shown not to have been harvested from within, removed from, or taken within the RNA, as applicable, by being stowed in a cabin, locker, or similar storage area prior to entering and during transit through the RNA, provided further that such vessel is in continuous transit through the RNA.
scope: (a)(14): 'Research Natural Area (RNA) at Dry Tortugas National Park means the 46-square-statute-mile area in the northwest portion of the park enclosed by connecting with straight lines the adjacent points of 82°51′ W and 24°36′ N, and 82°58′ W and 24°36′ N west to the park boundary, but excluding: (i) The designated anchorage; (ii) Garden Key, Bush Key and Long Key; or (iii) The central portion of Loggerhead key including the lighthouse and associated buildings.'
note: Checked 30 Sep 2026. (e)(1) 'Anchoring in the Research Natural Area (RNA) is prohibited.' (e)(2) 'All vessels in the RNA must use designated mooring buoys.' (h)(1): a Superintendent's permit is required for all non-commercial vessels whose occupants are engaged in recreational activities, including all activities in the RNA. (b)(3)(ii) to (v) also close the Garden Key moat, buoyed swim and snorkel areas, within 50 feet of the historic coaling docks, and helipad areas. Compendium (last updated 31 Aug 2026, secondary): no fishing from Bush Key; no fishing from the Garden Key dock when the ferry is docked; diving between sunset and sunrise outside 1 nm of the Garden Key Light needs a permit; no entering or exiting the water from the moat wall.

effect: Swimming, snorkeling and diving are closed within 100 feet of every marked navigational channel in the park, in three harbors and two harbor mouths, and in the Legare Anchorage box (25°29′N to 25°30′N, 80°07′W to 80°08′W).
excerpt: The following areas are closed to swimming, wading, snorkeling, and underwater diving: The Legare Anchorage within the rectangular area bounded by latitude 25°30 N and 25°29 N and longitude 80°08 W and 80°07 W; Boca Chita Key Harbor; Elliott Key Harbor; Convoy Point Harbor; Within the slow speed zone at the mouth/entrance of Boca Chita Key Harbor; Within the mouth/entrance of Elliott Key Harbor; Within one hundred feet (100') of all marked navigational channels
